findings.location: Compatibility matrix — "| macOS (APFS, case-insensitive default) | unknown | suite expected to pass; case-only moves rejected by the disk check — unverified (A10) |"
findings.problem: The row carries no decision: `unknown` is not a status an implementer or operator can act on, and the Notes cell hedges twice ("expected to pass", "unverified"). The compatibility checklist requires a status on every platform row.
findings.fix: Replace `unknown` with a committed status and back it with a named check: either "yes (unverified)" with Test strategy #12 made concrete for macOS (run one move round trip plus one case-only move and record the observed rejection as the A10 evidence), or "not exercised" stating the runner is not run there.

findings.location: Compatibility matrix — "| Windows (NTFS, `core.protectNTFS`) | unknown | never exercised in this repo's pipeline; name-legality rules untested |"
findings.problem: Same missing decision, and the Notes cell names a gap ("name-legality rules untested") that no validator rule and no Test strategy case addresses, so the row cannot resolve itself during implementation.
findings.fix: Pick the status as for macOS and make Test strategy #12 name the two Windows observations this design depends on — a move round trip, and the behavior of a `\`-separated or Windows-illegal `to`. If no one will run the pipeline on Windows, say so in the Notes cell instead of leaving `unknown`.

findings.location: Chosen design / Validator rule 1 — "repo-relative POSIX paths, normalized, no absolute path, no `.` or `..` segments"
findings.problem: "normalized" is undefined while every downstream check assumes `/`: rule 4 builds the revspec `<headBefore>:<from>`, the new `.git` rule is the string test "path === '.git' || path.startsWith('.git/'", and `stagePathAllowed` is regex-on-`/` (gates.ts:253,260). A reply emitting `src\old.ts` clears rule 1 (no `/`-separated `..`, no absolute marker) and then fails rule 4 with a confusing "not tracked at headBefore"; a `.git\config` endpoint escapes the `.git` string test and is caught only accidentally. The repo already normalizes the other way (`relative(repoDir, doc).split(/[\/]/).join('/')`, runner.ts:134).
findings.fix: Define normalization in one rule-1 clause: reject any `\` in either endpoint and compare with `path.posix` segment semantics; add one rejection case to Test strategy #2.

findings.location: Chosen design / Validator rule 1 — "Shape: repo-relative POSIX paths, normalized, no absolute path"
findings.problem: The shape list covers `.`/`..`/absolute but no per-OS name legality, while the Windows row itself says "name-legality rules untested". A Windows-reserved component (`CON`, `NUL`, trailing dot/space) validates and commits cleanly on the Linux reference platform; a `:` in a path additionally corrupts the `<headBefore>:<from>` revspec in rule 4, so it fails as an apparent git error rather than a validator message naming the pair.
findings.fix: Extend the same rule-1 sentence with a reserved/illegal-name check on each segment (one regex) plus one Test strategy #2 case — or state in the Windows Notes cell that name legality is operator-checked; today the text says untested without deciding which.

findings.location: Chosen design / Validator rule 6 — "all `from`s distinct, all `to`s distinct" … "so the list is a matching on disjoint paths and apply order is irrelevant"
findings.problem: Distinctness is string-distinct, which is not disjointness on a case-insensitive checkout — the platform class the macOS/Windows rows name. Two `to`s differing only in case pass rules 5 and 6, then the second pair's per-pair "re-check `to` absent" trips inside `applyMoves`: the list rolls back as `moves-apply-failed` (environmental class, fresh session) instead of the cheap in-attempt nudge, and the "apply order is irrelevant" claim is false as written.
findings.fix: In rule 6, compare endpoint sets case-folded when the checkout is case-insensitive (reusing the `existsSync` probe rule 5 already uses), or state the unconditional rule that case-insensitively colliding endpoints are rejected everywhere.

findings.location: Compatibility matrix — "| Repository spanning mount points | partial | `rename(2)` fails `EXDEV` (A8): the pair fails at apply, the list rolls back, the stage fails with `moves-apply-failed` |"
findings.problem: The row describes a specific path through `applyMoves` that no test names; Test strategy #5 and #11 exercise a generic mid-list failure, not the cross-mount case, so the "partial" status has no observation behind it.
findings.fix: Name it in #5: a pair whose `to` parent sits on a different mount (e.g. a tmpfs under the tmpRepo worktree).

findings.location: Compatibility matrix — "| Node ≥ 22.12 (tools/orchestration/package.json:30-32) | yes | no new runtime dependency: `fs.renameSync` plus the existing git helper |"
findings.problem: The matrix pins the runtime floor but not the git binary floor the design newly leans on: `git status --no-optional-locks*` needs git ≥ 2.19, and rename detection defaults and `core.ignoreCase` behavior are version-dependent.
findings.fix: Add one matrix row "git ≥ <floor>", or one clause in the Node row naming the assumed git floor.

findings.location: Chosen design — Read-only git for implement/fix/test-update seats (item 5): "`git status --no-optional-locks*` (the pinned form avoids the index-refresh side effect and the lock contention with the runner's own git calls, A6)"
findings.problem: The pinned form is the wrong spelling. git(1)'s synopsis places --no-optional-locks among the options that precede <command>, it appears in none of git-status's own OPTIONS, and git-status's BACKGROUND REFRESH section (and this run's own 01-research.md) spell the remedy `git --no-optional-locks status`. As pinned, the only allowed `git status` form is one git rejects with a fatal unknown option, so the goal "the coder and test-engineer seats can run `git status`" is not delivered as written and the claim that the pin avoids the index refresh is false for that flag position.
findings.fix: Replace the allow entry with `git --no-optional-locks status*` (the documented git(1) spelling); deny refinements and the rest of the allowlist unchanged.

findings.location: Chosen design — Read-only git section: "review seats already run the same three of four, code-correctness.md:27-31"
findings.problem: The cited file and every other agent config carry exactly two of the four named commands: `git diff*` and `git log*` (design-review seats only `git diff*`); `git show*` and `git status*` appear in no agent definition. The precedent holds, the count does not.
findings.fix: Change to "the same two of four (`git diff*`, `git log*)".

findings.location: Chosen design — Validator rule 7: "the realpath of `from` and of `to`'s nearest existing ancestor stay inside the repo's realpath"
findings.problem: 'Nearest existing ancestor' deliberately tolerates a `to` whose parent directory does not exist: such a pair passes every pre-flight rule, then deterministically fails at apply with renameSync ENOENT, is classified `moves-apply-failed` as 'the model's reply was fine, the failure is environmental' — false for this case — and bypasses the in-attempt nudge path, burning a fresh session and (for fix) a budget unit. ADR-005 item 2's own standard is to check everything before touching anything, and this is a pure pre-touch disk check.
findings.fix: Add to rule 5: "`to`'s parent directory exists on disk"; add the case to Test strategy #2's one-case-per-rule list.

findings.location: Assumption register A13: "saveState re-validates | verified | tools/orchestration/src/pipeline/state-store.ts:145-155"
findings.problem: Lines 145-155 are loadState's version gate and safeParse; saveState's re-validation is at 178-184. The claim is true but the cited range does not cover the saveState half of the row.
findings.fix: Cite state-store.ts:145-155, 178-184.

findings.location: Assumption register A6: "`git status` refreshes the index by default | verified | https://git-scm.com/docs/git-log, https://git-scm.com/docs/git-diff, https://git-scm.com/docs/git-config"
findings.problem: The claim is true (git-status BACKGROUND REFRESH) but none of the three cited pages carries it; the source is git(1)/git-status(1).
findings.fix: Add https://git-scm.com/docs/git (or git-status) to the row's basis.

findings.location: Chosen design — "Read-only git for implement/fix/test-update seats (item 5)": "Precondition, enforced: `stagePathAllowed` gains, as its first line, `path === '.git' || path.startsWith('.git/') → false`"
findings.problem: The mechanism named as enforcement of item 5's precondition cannot observe or undo the write it is meant to stop. Per A4 the sweep's entire input is git's dirty-path list, and `.git/**` is by construction never a dirty path; and "restores violations from `headBefore`" cannot restore `.git/config`, which has no blob at `headBefore`. A stage that writes `.git/config` (A7 says it can today) is neither blocked nor reverted: the plant survives the attempt boundary and is re-read by every later git call including the runner's own (`git add -A` in `commitStage`, the sweep's status/diff, the new rule-4 `git cat-file`), turning config keys into execution at runner privilege, outside the agent permission model. The only mechanism that can actually prevent the write — the agent-config `edit` deny — is demoted in the text to "The advisory mirror". Test strategy #4 only asserts the predicate returns false, which holds whether or not the write is preventable.
findings.fix: Make the harness-side control load-bearing: name the OpenCode `edit`/`write` deny on `.git` and `.git/**` in `coder.md` and `test-engineer.md` as the enforcement and delete the word "advisory"; keep the `stagePathAllowed` first line as the validator endpoint rule and defense-in-depth only; replace test #4's predicate assertion with an attempt-and-observe test that a stage write to `.git/config` is refused. If the harness cannot be shown to deny that path, item 5 does not ship in this change.

findings.location: Chosen design — item 5 paragraph: "with `.git/config` unwritable, `diff.external`, `core.pager`, `core.hooksPath`, and `diff.*.textconv` drivers cannot be planted" (and A6, which grounds it)
findings.problem: The closed-lever list omits `core.fsmonitor`, the config sink behind the current class of git-config execution advisories, which fires on an index refresh rather than on a flag — and the design's only stated defence for `git status` is that `--no-optional-locks` "avoids the index-refresh side effect", while the newly allowed `git diff*`/`git show*` are exactly the calls that refresh the index. With argv vetting Deferred, every config-triggered sink is protected solely by the config write-deny of the finding above, so an incomplete list there is an unmitigated execution path, and the argv deny list (`--output*`, `--ext-diff*`, `--textconv*`) covers none of it. Risks row 1's mitigation is also mismatched: "worktree landings are swept and land in visible commits" mitigates a rogue write, not a rogue execution, which leaves nothing in the worktree to sweep.
findings.fix: Add `core.fsmonitor` (and `filter.<driver>.clean`/`smudge`, `core.sshCommand`) to A6 and to the closed-lever list; restate Risks row 1's mitigation as the config-write deny plus a hostile `.git/config` fixture asserting the newly allowed commands do not execute it; state explicitly that the argv deny list is best-effort, not the control.

findings.location: Chosen design — "Reply field": "`moves: z.array(MovePairSchema).default([])`"
findings.problem: The untrusted list carries no bound — no maximum pair count and no maximum path length — while rule 4 spends a `git cat-file` subprocess plus `existsSync`/`realpath` per pair and rule 6's "no listed path is a path-prefix of another" is quadratic in list size. A reply steered by injected content makes finalize burn unbounded subprocess and CPU work before any rejection (security checklist: size limits on untrusted data).
findings.fix: `z.array(MovePairSchema).default([]).max(N)` plus `.max(len)` on `from`/`to`, so an oversize list fails at `safeParse` on the same invalid-reply path; extend Test strategy #1 with the over-limit case.

findings.location: Chosen design — "Validator" rule 1: "Shape: repo-relative POSIX paths, normalized, no absolute path, no `.` or `..` segments, `from !== to`"
findings.problem: Shape is checked but the character class is not: NUL, control characters, or a backslash survive rule 1 and reach `existsSync`, `git cat-file`, and `realpath`, where spawn/fs throw `ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE`. The design routes only a validator-returned issue to "`invalid-reply: moves — <issue>`", so a throw escapes the nudge/retry path and crashes finalize instead of failing the reply — the fail-open case the Goals forbid. Backslash is also platform-dependent: splitting on `/` alone makes `..\..\x` one legal segment on Windows, with rule 7's realpath as the only backstop.
findings.fix: Tighten rule 1 to a single allow-pattern that rejects NUL, control characters, and `\`, so no exotic string reaches a syscall, and wrap the `validateMoves` call in a catch that converts any throw into the same `invalid-reply: moves` branch; add both cases to Test strategy #2.

findings.location: Chosen design — "Apply": "`moves.applyMoves(repoDir, moves)`, called from `finalizeStage`" with only "re-check `to` absent"
findings.problem: Rules 4–7 (tracked at `headBefore`, on-disk existence, containment) are not re-checked at apply time — `applyMoves` is not even passed `headBefore` — while `moves` is persisted into the checkpoint (A13; Rollout 2's "in-flight and old checkpoints re-parse unchanged"). A resume that re-enters finalize with an already-accepted reply therefore applies a list whose state-dependent rules were evaluated against a stale `headBefore` and stale disk state; the design reasons about a crash between apply and commit but not between reply acceptance and apply.
findings.fix: Pass `headBefore` into `applyMoves` and re-run the state-dependent rules (4–7) as a single guard immediately before the first rename, making apply the one authoritative validation call site instead of parse-time only.

findings.location: Chosen design — "Apply": "completed renames are rolled back in reverse — exact because pairs are disjoint"
findings.problem: The rollback itself can fail (`rename(2)` fails `EISDIR`/`EXDEV`/`EINVAL` per A8, or `EACCES`/`ENOSPC`), and the design specifies nothing for that case. The result is exactly the half-applied list the Goals promise to prevent, and the documented recovery launders it: "the next attempt re-captures `headBefore`" makes the damaged state the baseline, so a partially applied move set can be committed by a later stage.
findings.fix: Emit a distinct `moves-rollback-failed` outcome that escalates to the operator instead of starting attempt 2 on a known-damaged worktree, and add a Test strategy #5 case where a rollback rename fails.

findings.location: Compatibility matrix — "Node ≥ 22.12 (tools/orchestration/package.json:30-32) | yes"
findings.problem: The runtime floor predates published Node 22.x security releases, including the permission-model path-traversal and `fs.realpathSync` permission-check fixes (22.22.0, 22.23.4). No unfixed advisory applies to a dependency named here, so this is not a blocker, but rule 7's containment leans on realpath semantics and the Deferred hand-off to "OS/sandbox-level protection" should not assume Node's `--permission` model is sound. No minimum `git` version is pinned anywhere despite the design relying on `git cat-file`, `-M` rename detection, and config-sink behavior.
findings.fix: State a patched minimum Node (e.g. 22.23.4) and a minimum `git` version in that row, and add one line to the sandbox Deferred noting that Node's permission model is not an acceptable substitute for harness or OS enforcement.

findings.location: Chosen design → Validator, rule 4 — "`from` is a tracked **file** at `headBefore` (`git cat-file -t <headBefore>:<from>` equals `blob` — this is the file-only rule)" [new]
findings.problem: The validator is specified as one git subprocess per endpoint: `git cat-file` per `from` (rule 4) plus a second headBefore membership query per `to` (rule 5), plus `existsSync`/`realpath` per pair. Run 004's motivating payload (23 pairs, A12) is ~46 subprocess spawns per validation pass, and the pass re-runs on every nudge cycle and again in attempt 2 (Wiring into retry), so a list needing three nudges across two attempts costs several hundred spawns. It sits in finalize/reply validation, not on a keystroke path, so this is minor rather than major, but the design never acknowledges the per-pair spawn cost and leaves the obvious batching unspecified.
findings.fix: Read headBefore once per validation pass instead of per pair: `git cat-file --batch` fed all `<headBefore>:<path>` endpoint queries through one process, or one `git ls-tree -r --name-only <headBefore>` snapshot held in a Set. This replaces the per-pair `git cat-file -t` in rule 4 and the per-`to` tracked lookup in rule 5 — same answers, one spawn per pass.

findings.location: Chosen design → Reply field + Validator rule 6 — "`moves: z.array(MovePairSchema).default([])`" and "no listed path is a path-prefix of another" [new]
findings.problem: The list length is unbounded — nothing caps the array, so n is model-controlled — and the prefix rule as written is naturally a pairwise scan, i.e. O(n²) in n for the disjointness/containment bookkeeping. Nothing bounds the blast radius of a pathological list (thousands of pairs) beyond the reply's own token size.
findings.fix: Bound it at the schema: `z.array(MovePairSchema).max(N).default([])` with N stated (a few hundred comfortably covers run 004's 23), and make rule 6 non-quadratic by sorting the normalized paths once and comparing each path only against its sorted neighbours, replacing the pairwise scan rather than adding to it.

findings.location: Compatibility matrix → "Repository spanning mount points" row — "`rename(2)` fails `EXDEV` (A8): the pair fails at apply, the list rolls back, the stage fails with `moves-apply-failed`" [new]
findings.problem: A statically-detectable condition is routed through the most expensive failure path in the design. `moves-apply-failed` deliberately drops the `invalid-reply` prefix (Apply: "so attempt 2 starts a fresh session"), so a cross-mount pair costs a full rollback of up to n−1 renames, then a fresh no-context session that re-derives the stage's whole reply, then escalation — and a fresh inference session is the dominant cost in this system. Rule 7 already realpaths `from` and `to`'s nearest existing ancestor, so the condition is knowable at validation for free.
findings.fix: Extend rule 7 to compare `statSync(from).dev` against the `dev` of `to`'s nearest existing ancestor and fail as `invalid-reply: moves` (the cheap nudge path); keep the apply-time `EXDEV` handling as the race guard rather than the first line of detection.

findings.location: Wiring into retry / Rollout 4 — "The in-attempt nudge loop is the cheap correction path" [new]
findings.problem: The document's cost claims are asserted, never quantified: "cheap" has no bound attached (the nudge cap it leans on is existing behavior cited as A2 but never numbered), and no section states the expected added finalize cost at the run-004 baseline size. Rollout 4's dogfood criteria are outcome-only ("no `operatorForce`/…", "land as `R` entries"), so nothing would notice if the new path made finalize slower — e.g. if the per-pair spawn cost scaled with a larger move set. There is no latency/cost budget line in the document, so this checklist item could not be evaluated.
findings.fix: One sentence in Apply or Rollout 1 stating the per-stage cost model after the batching fix — one headBefore read + n `renameSync` calls + n stat checks, target under a second for a run-004-sized 23-pair list — plus the existing max-nudges-per-attempt number that bounds "cheap". This does not re-open the budget-burn decision closed at r0 OQ6: one code-budget unit per full failed attempt stands; only its bound is unstated.

findings.location: Chosen design → Read-only git — "`git status --no-optional-locks*` … `git log*`, `git diff*`, `git show*`" [new]
findings.problem: The only cost-pinned form is `status`; the other three are granted in unbounded spellings, and `git log -p` / `git log --follow` over full history is the most output- and CPU-hungry invocation available inside a stage turn, landing straight in agent context. Precedent exists (review seats already run the same three of four), so this is preference, not a defect.
findings.fix: Optionally mirror the `status` treatment with a one-line prompt/config note that log/diff calls be bounded (`-n`, path-scoped), the same way `--no-optional-locks` was pinned for cost reasons.

findings.location: Options considered, "Allow directory moves" — "File-only removes that entire rule class."
findings.problem: The rationale overclaims against the design's own validator rule 6, which keeps "no listed path is a path-prefix of another" — a superset of the self-containment check the sentence says is removed, and still needed for file pairs (e.g. to1=a with to2=a/b). An implementer could read the rationale as license to drop the prefix clause. Fix: narrow the claim to what file-only actually removes — cascade rules for children and the per-child tracked-at-headBefore check — and note the path-prefix disjointness clause stays in rule 6 for file pairs.
findings.fix: Replace "File-only removes that entire rule class." with "File-only removes the cascade rules and the per-child tracked-at-headBefore check; rule 6's path-prefix disjointness clause stays for file pairs."

reply.summary: Every open major was consumed by changing the design, not appending to it: the `git status` allow entry becomes the documented `git --no-optional-locks status*` form (Goals and Revision log reworded to match); item 5's enforcement moves to the agent-config `edit` deny on `.git`/`.git/**` with the `stagePathAllowed` line demoted to the validator's endpoint rule/defense-in-depth (the word "advisory" deleted, #4's predicate assertion deleted, replaced by an attempt-and-observe plus hostile-`.git/config`-fixture ship gate in #13); A6 and the closed-lever list now name `core.fsmonitor`, `core.sshCommand`, and `filter.<driver>.clean/smudge`, and Risks 1 restates the mitigation as the config-write deny with the argv denials marked best-effort; the macOS row becomes `yes (unverified)` behind a concrete #12 and the Windows row `not exercised`; validator rule 1 is now one allow-check (`path.posix` semantics, no `\`/NUL/control/`:`, no reserved names) with rule 5 requiring `to`'s parent on disk and rule 6 comparing endpoints case-folded, so containment's "nearest existing ancestor" and the case-dependent "apply order" hedge are gone; `applyMoves` takes `headBefore` and re-runs rules 4–7 as the single pre-rename guard (deleting the per-pair `to` re-check), a failed rollback becomes `moves-rollback-failed` escalating to the operator, the reply list/paths gain `.max` bounds, and the matrix adds a `git ≥ 2.16` floor row with a patched-Node note and a Deferred note that Node's `--permission` model is not a substitute. Net +2 lines (335→337), because three findings required new pinned artifacts — the git floor row, the `.git/config` ship-gate test, and rule-level cases in Test strategy #2 — offset by deleting the advisory-mirror passage, the #4 predicate assertion, the CLI-surface deferral, the duplicated budget and linked-worktree claims, and six sentences of redundant Options/Context/Sweep prose.
reply.commitMessage: docs: revise moves proposal for r1 design reviews

findings.location: Chosen design / Validator rule 2 + Read-only git — "no endpoint `.git`-denied (see Read-only git — the same `stagePathAllowed` rule)" and "`stagePathAllowed` gains, as its first line, `path === '.git' || path.startsWith('.git/') → false` (gates.ts:260)"
findings.problem: The `.git` guard is a case-sensitive string test while the row that makes it load-bearing is now a supported row (macOS `yes (unverified)`). On a case-insensitive checkout `to = '.GIT/hooks/pre-commit'` clears rule 1 (clean POSIX shape), rule 2 (`.GIT` ≠ `.git` as a string), rule 3 (`stagePathAllowed` is true for implement/fix; the new first line does not match), rule 5 (`existsSync` false for an absent hook, no blob at headBefore, and parent `.GIT/hooks` resolves to the real `.git/hooks`), and rules 6–7. `applyMoves` then renames a worktree file into the real git directory — invisible to the sweep (A4: `.git/**` is never a dirty path) and executed by the runner's own next `git commit`. The r1 revision sharpens this: item 5's enforcement moved to the harness-side `edit` deny, which constrains agent writes only and cannot constrain a runner-side rename, so rule 2 is the sole control on this path; and A10's new claim "nothing else in the design depends on the checkout being case-sensitive" is contradicted. r1 finding #3's `\` vector on this same guard is closed; the case vector is not. (new)
findings.fix: Make rule 2's test and the `stagePathAllowed` first line case-folded — `path.toLowerCase() === '.git' || path.toLowerCase().startsWith('.git/')` — replacing the exact-case comparison; it cannot reject a legitimate name, since a segment equal to `.git` ignoring case cannot coexist with `.git`. Add `.GIT/hooks/pre-commit` to Test strategy #2's rejection list, pinned on Linux.

findings.location: Chosen design / Validator rule 6 — "all `from`s distinct and all `to`s distinct compared case-folded, no `to` equals any `from`, and no listed path is a path-prefix of another — which rejects … case-only collisions"
findings.problem: The case-folded qualifier grammatically binds only the two distinctness clauses; the `to`-vs-`from` and path-prefix clauses remain string-exact. A single case-only pair (`README.md` → `readme.md`) is rejected nowhere on the reference platform: rule 5's `existsSync` guard — the rule it calls "the case-insensitive-checkout guard, A10" — is inert on case-sensitive ext4, rule 1's `from !== to` is exact, and `applyMoves` lands it as an `R` entry. That makes the Risks mitigation "Rule 5's disk check rejects case-only endpoints and rule 6 rejects case-folded collisions on every platform" false for the reference platform, sits under the Deferred entry that presumes case-only renames are currently rejected, and leaves "apply order is irrelevant" unproven for a list with `A→B` and `a→C`. Test strategy #2's "duplicate endpoints including case-only collisions" pins duplicates within a list, not the lone case-only pair. (re-raised: my r1 rule-6 finding, partially closed)
findings.fix: Scope it in one clause — "every comparison in this rule is case-folded" — replacing the clause-attached qualifier, and add one Test strategy #2 case: a lone `README.md` → `readme.md` pair rejected on Linux.

findings.location: Test strategy #5 / Compatibility matrix "Repository spanning mount points | partial" — "a pair whose `to` parent is on another mount (tmpfs under the worktree) fails `EXDEV`"
findings.problem: The `partial` row now names an observation, but creating a tmpfs requires root/`CAP_SYS_ADMIN`, which the vitest tmpRepo suite cannot assume; if CI cannot mount, the row keeps an evidence-less status under a new name. (new)
findings.fix: Name the runner of that case the way #12 does for macOS ("operator-run, mount required"), or gate it on mount capability so it skips visibly instead of disappearing.

findings.location: Chosen design — Read-only git for implement/fix/test-update seats (item 5) — "The enforcement is the harness-side write deny: `coder.md` and `test-engineer.md` gain `edit` denies on `.git` and `.git/**` … It is load-bearing, because the sweep cannot see or undo a config plant"
findings.problem: re-raised? no — new. The r1 rewrite moved item 5's enforcement onto the agent-config permission layer and demoted the runner-side check to "Defense in depth", but this repo states twice that the permission layer is not the control: gates.ts:256-258 ("Agent-config permissions are only advisory (a model can route around them via subagents), so the runner enforces this matrix deterministically") and independence.ts's header ("permissions alone did not hold, so the runner verifies after the fact"). The design's own sentence concedes the deterministic half is blind here (`.git/**` is never a dirty path), and the `stagePathAllowed` line it keeps only runs over move endpoints and sweep output — never over an `edit` call. So the config plant that Options 1 cites as the reason to refuse any agent git access is left with no deterministic control while the allowlist re-opens exactly that lever, and Test strategy #13's fixture exercises only the direct write the advisory fence already claims to stop.
findings.fix: Make the enforcement the mechanism the repo already uses for fences permissions do not hold: extend the existing runner-side tool-call audit (`auditSessionIndependence`, independence.ts, called at runner.ts:839-849 — "The permissions say so; this checks up on it") with a `.git`-segment matcher over completed write/edit tool calls that fails the attempt, and keep the agent-config deny as the advisory mirror (what r0 said). Alternatively register "the harness `edit` deny cannot be routed around by the stage's own tools or subagents" as an unverified assumption and make #13's fixture use the route gates.ts:257 names.

findings.location: Chosen design — Apply — "Immediately before the first rename it re-runs validator rules 4–7 as one guard, so a resume re-entering finalize on a checkpointed reply never applies against a stale `headBefore` or stale disk"
findings.problem: The premise is false for this codebase: `finalizeStage` has one call site, `executeStage`, immediately after a fresh `executeInference` (runner.ts:1070-1081), and resume re-runs the stage from inference (resumePipeline → drive → runWithRetry → executeStage, runner.ts:1453-1484); the checkpoint stores no replayable reply. The real window the guard closes is validate-at-inference → apply-at-finalize (which the Risks row states correctly). The stated premise is also self-defeating: were finalize re-entered on an already-applied list, rules 4–7 would reject it forever (rule 4 wants `from` on disk, rule 5 wants `to` absent), contradicting "A crash between apply and commit converges on resume".
findings.fix: Restate the guard's rationale as the inference→finalize window the Risks row already names, and delete the checkpointed-reply clause.

findings.location: Chosen design — Apply — "Immediately before the first rename it re-runs validator rules 4–7 as one guard"
findings.problem: The guard's failure class is the only exit in that paragraph left unclassified: rename errors get `moves-apply-failed` (attempt 2, fresh session, worktree preserved) and rollback errors get `moves-rollback-failed` (stops at the operator), but a guard refusal names no outcome, no preserved-worktree state, and no test class — #5 pins that the guard refuses without naming the result, and #6 enumerates only the other three. The refusal also happens after the reply was accepted, where the `invalid-reply:` nudge path is no longer available.
findings.fix: One clause: a guard refusal takes the same `moves-apply-failed` outcome and preserved-worktree state as a rename error; pin it in Test strategy #5/#6.

findings.location: Chosen design — Read-only git (item 5) vs Options considered — "If Test strategy #13 cannot show the harness refusing a `.git/config` write, item 5 does not ship in this change." against "**Land `moves` without item 5.** Rejected: the ADR decided item 5"
findings.problem: The gate's fallback is exactly the option the Options section rejects, and ADR-005 item 5 is decided, so the design leaves the ship-failure outcome undecided (whole change held, or `moves` lands with ADR-005 item 5 unimplemented?). Meanwhile the Goals bullet "The coder and test-engineer seats can run `git --no-optional-locks status`, `git log`, `git diff`, `git show` read-only" states the conditional outcome unconditionally.
findings.fix: Name the consequence in the same sentence — the change does not merge with item 5 unproven, or item 5 moves to a named follow-up with the ADR item left open — and qualify the Goals bullet to match.

findings.location: Chosen design — Validator rule 6 — "all `from`s distinct and all `to`s distinct compared case-folded"
findings.problem: On the case-sensitive reference platform two tracked files differing only by case (`src/a.ts`, `src/A.ts`) are distinct blobs at `headBefore` (rule 4 proves it), so a two-pair list over them is legal input that the validator now deterministically rejects as a reply error, burning a code-budget unit (A3). The rule is safe, hence not unsound, but the text does not say the Linux rejection is intended, so an implementer cannot tell rule from bug.
findings.fix: One clause stating the conservatism ("case-folded distinctness is enforced on every platform; a repo with case-variant filenames cannot move both in one reply"), or gate the fold on the checkout's `core.ignoreCase`.

findings.location: Assumption register A6 — "`core.fsmonitor` fires on an index refresh — which `git status`, `git diff`, and `git show` all perform by default, `git --no-optional-locks` aside"
findings.problem: The row's own basis supports two of the three: git-status(1) BACKGROUND REFRESH covers `git status`, and `diff.autoRefreshIndex` ("defaults to true … affects only git diff Porcelain") covers `git diff`; nothing cited documents an index refresh for `git show`, which by default compares commits/trees rather than the worktree. The row's conclusion is unaffected, but a `verified` row carries an unsupported sub-claim.
findings.fix: Drop "and `git show`" from that clause, or add the basis that shows the refresh for it.

findings.location: Chosen design — "Read-only git for implement/fix/test-update seats (item 5)": "An unwritable `.git/config` closes every config sink A6 names, `core.fsmonitor` — which fires on the index refresh these commands perform — included."
findings.problem: re-raised theme, new instance (arises from the r1 closure): git's exec-capable config is not one file. Sources are repo-local `.git/config`, `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config`, `~/.gitconfig`, `/etc/gitconfig`, and `include.path` reachable from any of them. The control r1 makes load-bearing cannot reach them: OpenCode matches `edit` resources as whole-value wildcards against the normalized Location-relative path, so `.git`/`.git/**` denies nothing outside the worktree, and the harness default has no `external_directory` ask/deny ("reads and edits outside the Location and worktree proceed without a prompt"), while the design's Options 2 says the runner's git helper "inherits ambient config". A stage writing `core.fsmonitor` into `~/.gitconfig` is stopped by nothing in the changed text, is invisible to the sweep (no worktree path, never dirty, no blob at `headBefore` — the paragraph's own argument), and executes at runner privilege on the runner's next `git status`/`git add -A`, surviving the attempt boundary. The Deferred item states the gap without closing it: "Hardening the runner's own git subprocess env (`GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM`, pinned `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`) — no follow-up yet; the `.git` write-deny closes the repo-local half."
findings.fix: Put the runner-side half on the load-bearing side: have `git()` set `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` and `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` to an empty file, or pass `-c core.fsmonitor=false -c safe.bareRepository=explicit` on the runner's calls (the shape of the 2026 fixes for this class); or deny the global/system config paths in `coder.md`/`test-engineer.md` and add them to Test #13's fixture. Either way replace "closes every config sink A6 names" with "closes the repo-local config source", matching the Deferred clause it leans on.

findings.location: Chosen design — item 5 paragraph: "`stagePathAllowed` gains, as its first line, `path === '.git' || path.startsWith('.git/') → false`" (and Compatibility matrix "git ≥ 2.16 … floor set by the global `--no-optional-locks`")
findings.problem: new: both named mechanisms are anchored at the worktree root, while the plant vector the design and ADR name is "the worktree" at large. `implement`/`fix` own everything but `tests/**` (A7), so a stage can write `<owned-dir>/.git/config` (or a bare `<owned-dir>.git/`). That path matches neither the whole-value patterns `.git`/`.git/**` nor `startsWith('.git/')`; it is in-ownership, so the sweep neither reverts nor deletes it (enforceOwnership only touches violations); and `commitStage`'s `git add -A` records it as a gitlink with only a warning ("adding embedded git repository"), giving the plant a committed marker that persists into later attempts. Every later superproject `git status`/`git diff` — including the runner's `dirtyFiles` — then consults that nested repository's config, where `core.fsmonitor` fires on the index refresh; git's only protection, `safe.bareRepository=explicit`, is opt-in and its default does not flip until Git 3.0. The stated floor removes even that: below 2.38 `safe.bareRepository` does not exist.
findings.fix: Make the rule a segment rule instead of a prefix rule: `p.split('/').includes('.git')` plus rejecting any `*.git` name in `stagePathAllowed`, and `**/.git/**` / `**/*.git` in the two agent configs. Raise the floor to `git ≥ 2.38` so the runner can set `safe.bareRepository=explicit`, and add a planted `<owned-dir>/.git/config` carrying `core.fsmonitor` to Test #13's hostile fixture as part of item 5's ship gate.

findings.location: Chosen design — item 5 allowlist paragraph: "the config-write deny above carries item 5 and argv vetting stays sandbox territory"; Risks row 1: "worktree landings land in visible commits"
findings.problem: new: the deny r1 makes load-bearing is scoped to the `edit` action's target path and cannot observe a write performed by an allowed shell command. A6 itself names `--output=<file>` on `git log`/`git diff` — a flag-only file write requiring no config — and the shipped allow patterns `git log*`/`git diff*` prefix-match any suffix, including `--output=.git/config` or an out-of-repo target; the harness warns that directory inference from shell command text is best-effort. With the argv refinements demoted to "best-effort hygiene, not the control", nothing in the changed text carries that class. Risks row 1's mitigation is false where the risk lands: a `.git/**` landing is, by the same paragraph's argument, never a dirty path and has no blob at `headBefore`, so it is neither swept nor visible in a commit.
findings.fix: Split the control by class in the text: config sinks → the config-write deny; flag-only write/exec levers → the `--output`/`--ext-diff`/`--textconv` denials, stated as load-bearing for that class and expressed as OpenCode `policies` hard-denies (applied after allow rules and saved approvals) rather than order-dependent agent-config refinements. Pin them in Test #13 by running `git log --output=.git/config` and `git diff --output=<owned path>` in an attempt and asserting refusal, on the same ship-gate footing as the `.git/config` write test. Delete "worktree landings land in visible commits" or scope it to paths that can be dirty.

findings.location: Chosen design — item 5 allowlist paragraph: "follow the existing prefix-pattern style"; A9: "OpenCode permission matching is prefix-pattern with most-specific-wins"
findings.problem: new: the documented model is whole-value wildcards with last-match-wins rule combination, not most-specific-wins. The `.git` deny and the argv refinements work only because they are appended after the broad allow (as coder.md happens to order them), so the mechanism description the design relies on for both the edit deny and the refinements is wrong.
findings.fix: Restate A9 as whole-value wildcards with last-match-wins, and state the ordering requirement — deny lines appended after the allows in `coder.md` and `test-engineer.md` — instead of relying on specificity.

findings.location: Test strategy #4 — sweep interaction (r1 rewrite of the r0 list)
findings.problem: new: the r1 rewrite dropped "`stagePathAllowed` is false for `.git` and `.git/**` for every stage" while demoting that rule to defense-in-depth, so the predicate's new first line has no direct assertion; #2 pins only the validator's use of it.
findings.fix: Restore one direct predicate assertion for the first line of `stagePathAllowed` in #4.

reply.summary: Every open major/minor is consumed by changing the design, not annotating it. Correctness #1 + security #1/#2/#3: item 5's enforcement moved off the advisory permission layer onto the repo's existing deterministic fence — `auditSessionIndependence` gains a case-folded `.git` segment matcher over completed write/edit/patch calls and shell command text (fails the attempt), `git()` sets `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM`/pinned `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`/`safe.bareRepository=explicit` (the Deferred runner-env bullet is deleted because it is now in scope), and `stagePathAllowed`'s first line becomes a case-folded `.git`-segment rule, which also answers compatibility #1 (`.GIT/hooks/pre-commit`) and the nested `<owned-dir>/.git/` gitlink plant; the ineffective `--output`/`--ext-diff`/`--textconv` deny refinements were deleted rather than defended, and the false Risks claim "worktree landings land in visible commits" is gone. Correctness #2: the non-existent checkpointed-reply resume path was deleted and the guard restated as the inference→finalize window. Correctness #3: guard refusal is now classified `moves-apply-failed`, pinned in #5/#6. Correctness #4 + Options 6: the ship gate's consequence is named (no half-landing; the change does not merge) and the Goals/Context bullets are qualified. Correctness #5 + compatibility #2: rule 6's case fold now covers every comparison, with the conservatism stated and a lone `README.md`→`readme.md` case pinned in #2. Nits: A6 drops `git show` and gains the multi-file config sources, A9 restated as whole-value wildcards with last-match-wins (deny-after-allow ordering), A10's blanket "nothing else depends on case sensitivity" clause deleted, #4 regains the direct predicate assertion, #5's EXDEV case is operator-run, the Node row says "current patched 22.x", the git floor moves to 2.38, and the `stageName` parameter was dropped from `applyMoves`. Diff is line-neutral (336 → 336): additions for the three deterministic controls were paid for by deleting the Deferred env bullet, the argv-refinement discussion, and duplicated Options/sweep prose.
reply.commitMessage: docs: revise runner-executed file moves proposal for review round 1

findings.location: Chosen design / Read-only git — "`git()` (runner.ts:106-112) stops reading ambient config: `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` at an empty file, `-c safe.bareRepository=explicit`"
findings.problem: new: this removes the only git-identity source most operator environments have and nothing replaces it. `commitStage` (runner.ts:288-309) authors every stage commit with a bare `git(repoDir, ['commit','-m',message])` — no `-c user.*`, no author/committer env — and today resolves identity from the ambient global/system config the new env suppresses; repo-local `.git/config` is still read (the paragraph itself scopes the agent denies as "advisory, scoped to the repo-local config source"), and no repo-local identity is pinned anywhere. On the reference platform with the usual `~/.gitconfig` identity, every stage commit fails `unable to auto-detect email address`: item 5's control breaks the runner's committer path. The same applies to the suite — every tmpRepo fixture pins identity only on its own setup calls (`execFileSync('git',['-c','user.name=f','-c','user.email=f@f',...])`, stage-lifecycle.test.ts:94 and the identical helper in reply-contract/funnel/parallel-*), so #8–#11's runner-side commits lose identity too, and #13's new fixture ("the runner's git calls ignore a hostile `~/.gitconfig`") pins exactly that behavior. The concern is not handed off: this diff deletes the former Deferred bullet on hardening the runner's git env, and no matrix or Risks row names the operator git-config dependency.
findings.fix: In the same sentence, pin identity on the authoring calls — `git()`'s env gains `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME`/`GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL`/`GIT_COMMITTER_NAME`/`GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL` (or the commit calls pass `-c user.name=… -c user.email=…`), replacing what the suppressed global config supplied — and extend #13 with the positive half: a stage commit succeeds in a tmpRepo with no global or system config present.

findings.location: Compatibility matrix (macOS row) + Test strategy #12 — "Test strategy #12 runs one move round trip and one case-only move there and records the observed rejection as the A10 evidence"
findings.problem: new (arises from the r2 rule-6 closure): A10 is the claim that the on-disk existence check (rule 5's `existsSync`) rejects a case-only endpoint on a case-insensitive checkout. Rule 6 now states "every comparison here is case-folded on every platform … rejecting … case-only moves (`README.md` → `readme.md`)", so a case-only pair is rejected before rule 5's disk check is reached, identically on Linux where #2 already pins it. The macOS observation can never discriminate `core.ignoreCase`, leaving the row's `yes (unverified)` and A10's `unverified` permanently unverifiable by the test named to verify them.
findings.fix: Change #12's second case to a pair rule 6 cannot see: `README.md` tracked, reply moves an unrelated `notes.md` → `readme.md`. On macOS rule 5's `existsSync` rejects it; on Linux the same pair is accepted and lands as a case-variant sibling — restate the macOS row's note as that contrast, which is the actual A10 evidence.

findings.location: Chosen design / Read-only git — "`stagePathAllowed` (gates.ts:260) returns `false` as its first line for any path with a case-folded `.git` segment or a segment ending in `.git`"
findings.problem: new: the second half is a suffix rule on the predicate the sweep applies to every dirty path for every stage (A4), so it is an ownership change beyond moves: any path with a segment ending in `.git` (`fixtures/upstream.git/**`, a file `notes.git`) becomes permanently unowned, an agent's edit there is silently reverted as if it were an ownership violation, and a validator endpoint there fails as a reply error on every platform. Nothing in the paragraph needs the suffix — both pinned cases (`.GIT/hooks/pre-commit`, `src/.git/config`) and the planted `<owned-dir>/.git/` gitlink have a segment equal to `.git` case-folded, and the bare-repo-named case the suffix would catch is the one the same paragraph assigns to `safe.bareRepository=explicit`. The config mirror `**/*.git` carries the same over-reach.
findings.fix: State the first line as case-folded segment equality — `false` for any path with a segment equal to `.git` ignoring case — and drop "or a segment ending in `.git`" together with the `**/*.git` deny; if the suffix is kept, name the plant that needs it and add a #4 case pinning that an edit to `<owned>/upstream.git` is a deliberate sweep revert.

findings.location: Chosen design — Read-only git (item 5) — "in the shape of its existing `transcripts` matcher, and a hit fails the attempt. It carries the plant the sweep cannot see or undo"
findings.problem: new. The control detects and fails the attempt but never neutralizes the payload, and the retry it triggers re-exposes the runner to it. auditSessionIndependence judges only messages at/after this attempt's prompt (independence.ts:46-50: "A retried attempt must not be failed again for reads an earlier attempt already paid for"), and an `independence violation:` failure is not resumable (retryInSameSession, runner.ts:1121-1126), so attempt 2 runs a fresh session in the SAME worktree with the plant still in `.git` — nothing restores it, which is the design's own premise ("`.git/**` is never dirty and has no blob at `headBefore`"). Attempt 2's finalize then runs `git add -A` (runner.ts:298) and `git commit -m` (307, no `--no-verify`) under the planted `.git/config` (core.fsmonitor, include.path) or a planted `.git/hooks/pre-commit`, executing at runner privilege, and no later attempt re-detects it. Test strategy #13 pins only "fails the attempt" — exactly the half that does not protect the run. The claim that the audit "carries the plant" is therefore false as written.
findings.fix: Make a `.git`-segment audit hit terminal for the run — escalate to the operator as `moves-rollback-failed` does, no attempt 2 — or name the neutralization step (delete/restore the detected `.git` path) that must happen before any later attempt; and extend #13 to assert the following attempt's runner `git commit` does not execute the plant.

findings.location: Chosen design — Read-only git (item 5) — "The enforcement is runner-side, because agent-config permissions are only advisory: a model can route around them (gates.ts:256-258, independence.ts)"
findings.problem: new (same theme as r1 #1, aimed at the new mechanism). The route those lines name is subagents — gates.ts:257: "a model can route around them via subagents" — and the chosen control is blind to it. auditSessionIndependence scans `lastSeen`, this attempt's own session message list (runner.ts:759-769, 839; independence.ts:10-12 "its own message list"). A9's newly cited docs state "A custom subagent uses its own permissions, not a subset of its parent's permissions" with a base policy of `{action:"*",resource:"*",effect:"allow"}`, and no config under .opencode/agents denies the subagent action for coder.md or test-engineer.md. So a `.git/config` write by a spawned subagent is invisible to the audit, invisible to the sweep, and ungoverned by the two configs' denies — the exact lever Options 1 uses to refuse agent git access. #13's three vectors all run in the seat's own session, so item 5's ship gate never exercises the route the justification cites.
findings.fix: Name how the attempt's child sessions are audited (the mechanism that enumerates them and feeds their completed write/edit/patch and shell parts into the same matcher), or add a subagent-performed `.git` write to #13 and, if uncoverable, record the subagent route as an explicit uncovered vector instead of claiming runner-side enforcement over "the plant the sweep cannot see or undo".

findings.location: Chosen design — Validator rule 7 — "rule 2's `.git` test runs on those resolved paths too"
findings.problem: new. Combined with the new predicate "any path with a case-folded `.git` segment or a segment ending in `.git`", running the test over absolute resolved paths rejects every endpoint whenever an ancestor of the checkout carries such a segment. The bare-clone-with-worktrees layout (`~/src/project.git/wt-feature`) is exactly the linked-worktree case the Compatibility matrix marks `yes` and #13 exercises via `git worktree add`; there every move fails rule 7, so the feature is unusable rather than merely `.git`-refusing. The planted-symlink case the clause exists for is already caught by the containment clause.
findings.fix: State that the segment test runs on the resolved path made relative to the repo's realpath, with containment remaining the absolute check.

findings.location: Chosen design — Read-only git (item 5) — "`-c safe.bareRepository=explicit`, so the config sources outside the repo that A6 names and a nested repo planted in the worktree never execute at runner privilege"
findings.problem: new. The nested-repo half is mis-attributed: safe.bareRepository (introduced in git 2.38, so the new floor row's basis holds) governs whether git will operate on a bare repository it discovers at the invocation's cwd, and `git()` already pins `cwd: repoDir` (runner.ts:106-112), so a nested repo in the worktree is never the discovered repository with or without the flag. Consequently #13's "the runner's git calls ignore … a nested bare repo" fixture passes whether or not the flag ships, so a control that both the enforcement paragraph and the Compatibility floor rest on is pinned by a test that cannot fail.
findings.fix: Attribute the nested-repo half to the pinned cwd and keep the flag claim to the ambient-config half; either drop the flag from the sentence and the 2.38 floor rationale, or make #13's case a runner git call whose cwd is inside the planted bare repo so the flag is actually exercised.

findings.location: Chosen design — Read-only git (item 5) — "The two agent configs mirror it as `edit` denies on `.git`, `.git/**`, `**/.git/**` and `**/*.git`"
findings.problem: new. Under the whole-value wildcard matching A9 now records (`*` matches zero or more characters including `/`), `**/*.git` denies only paths that end in `.git`, so the mirror does not express the predicate's "a segment ending in `.git`" for its children (e.g. `src/mirror.git/config` remains permitted by the config); and the docs make path matching case-insensitive only on Windows, so the `.GIT/hooks/pre-commit` refusal the paragraph attributes to the mirror is runner-side alone.
findings.fix: One clause: the advisory mirror covers the `.git` dir/pointer and nested `.git/` dirs; the `*.git`-segment and case-folded halves exist only in `stagePathAllowed`.

findings.location: Chosen design — "Read-only git for implement/fix/test-update seats (item 5)": "in the shape of its existing `transcripts` matcher, and a hit fails the attempt"
findings.problem: new: the audit detects a `.git` plant but never contains it, and the shipped retry path re-exposes it. An audit hit fails the attempt; nothing removes the planted `.git/config` (the design's own A4 says the sweep can neither see nor undo `.git/**`). An `independence violation:` failure is not `invalid-reply`, so attempt 2 runs a fresh session on the same worktree (runner.ts:836-838, retryInSameSession 1121-1126), and attempt 2's audit scans only messages since its own `auditStart` (independence.ts `since`), so the attempt-1 write is never re-detected. If attempt 2 succeeds, finalize's `dirtyFiles` `git status` and `commitStage`'s `git add -A` are runner `git()` calls, and the pinned env (GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, safe.bareRepository) does not stop git from reading the repo-local `.git/config` — the planted `core.fsmonitor` fires on the index refresh at runner privilege. If both attempts fail, the plant persists in the operator's checkout and executes on every later git command. Chain: plant in attempt 1 → attempt 1 fails audit → clean attempt 2 → the commit executes the plant at runner privilege; #13 as written passes this chain because it asserts only that the attempt fails.
findings.fix: Name the containment step beside "fails the attempt": a `.git`-matcher hit escalates the stage to the operator immediately — no attempt 2, no finalize until the plant is cleared — and extend #13's ship gate to pin containment: the hostile fixture is an fsmonitor that touches a marker file, and after the audit-failed attempt the runner's next git call must not create the marker.

findings.location: Chosen design — item 5 paragraph: "agent-config permissions are only advisory: a model can route around them (gates.ts:256-258, independence.ts)"
findings.problem: new: the design demotes the config denies to advisory using the repo's own rationale that the bypass route is subagents (gates.ts:256-258: "a model can route around them via subagents"), but the audit it promotes to carrier sees only the attempt's own session — "the completed tool calls and shell commands in its own message list" (independence.ts:10-11; the runner passes one session's `lastSeen`, runner.ts:757, 839). A write completed inside a subagent's child session is not in that list; the base permission policy allows `*` and neither agent config denies `subagent`. The exact bypass the design cites to justify the audit therefore slips past both the advisory deny and the carrier, and the surviving plant then executes per the first finding.
findings.fix: State the audit's session scope: either audit subagent sessions spawned by the attempt, or deny `subagent` launch for the two move-emitting seats (the doc's own note that a `policies` entry hard-denies after rules and saved approvals makes that enforceable), and pin the chosen route in #13 — a subagent write to `src/.git/config` must fail.

findings.location: Risks row 1: "The audit's case-folded `.git` matcher fails the attempt for the write however it was spelled"
findings.problem: new: overclaimed — the matcher is a `.git` whole-segment match, so an allowed command writing a git config file outside the worktree (`git log --output=~/.gitconfig`, an XDG config path) matches nothing: the segment is `.gitconfig`, the `**/.git/**`/`**/*.git` edit denies are Location-relative whole-value patterns with no `external_directory` ask/deny in the harness default, and the sweep cannot see outside the worktree. Impact is contained — `git()`'s pinned env keeps it from executing at runner privilege and agent-privilege exec is the Deferred sandbox line — but a host-persistent config plant escapes every control this change ships while the mitigation sentence asserts it is caught.
findings.fix: Scope the claim: "fails the attempt for any `.git`-segment write, however spelled; out-of-worktree config landings are contained by `git()`'s pinned env and left to the Deferred sandbox line" — or extend the matcher with a `.gitconfig` segment case and pin it in #13.

reply.summary: Net -1 line (335 vs 336). Correctness/security majors on the plant: the `.git`-segment audit hit is no longer detect-and-retry — it ends the stage as `git-plant-detected` escalating to the operator with no attempt 2 and no finalize (the retry-over-the-plant path is deleted), and #13's ship gate now asserts containment via an fsmonitor marker the runner's next git call must not create. Correctness/security subagent major: the two seat configs append a `subagent` deny (A9 extended to the Actions table), and #13 pins a subagent-launched `src/.git/config` write plus refused launches. Compatibility major on lost git identity: `git()`'s env now pins a fixed pipeline author/committer, the git row records the operator-config independence, and #13 adds the positive case (a stage commit in a tmpRepo with no global/system config). Correctness minor on rule 7: the segment test runs on the resolved path made relative to the repo realpath, containment stays absolute, so a `project.git`-ancestor linked worktree stays legal. Correctness minor on `safe.bareRepository`: the flag sentence is scoped to outside-repo config sources and the nested bare repo is attributed to `git()`'s pinned `cwd`.
