Compatibility minor on macOS evidence: #12 and the macOS row use `notes.md` → `readme.md` against a tracked `README.md`, the only pair that discriminates rule 5's disk check from rule 6's fold; A10 reworded to match. Security minor: Risks row 1 is scoped to `.git`-segment writes with out-of-worktree config landings routed to the Deferred sandbox bullet (also owned there per the correctness FYI). FYI items consumed without new text: non-goal narrowed to git *write* access, matcher narrowed to call paths rather than payload text. Offsetting deletions: the `.git`-suffix sub-rule, the `**/*.git` deny, the duplicated sweep-crash and half-landing sentences, and the argv/Deferred duplication.
reply.commitMessage: docs: make .git audit hits terminal and pin runner commit identity in moves proposal

findings.location: Compatibility matrix (macOS row) + Test strategy #12 + Validator rule 5 — "macOS rejects it at rule 5's disk check where Linux lands a case-variant sibling — that contrast is the A10 evidence"
findings.problem: new (arises from the r3 closure of my round-1 #12 finding): #12 now pins, as the reference platform's expected behavior, a working tree that tracks two paths differing only in case (README.md plus the newly moved readme.md). Rule 5 refuses `to` only when it exists on disk — a fold performed by the filesystem, so it fires only on a case-insensitive checkout — or is tracked at headBefore, and rule 6's fold compares only paths inside one reply, so nothing on Linux refuses the pair; `git add -A` then commits a tree with a case-only collision. The same row claims macOS `yes`, and a checkout of that commit on a case-insensitive filesystem cannot represent both entries, so a Linux stage silently lands a commit that breaks a platform the matrix calls supported — the exact "case-insensitive checkouts behave unexpectedly" hazard the risk table tracks.
findings.fix: Make rule 5's tracked comparison case-folded on every platform — refuse `to` when its case-folded form equals any path tracked at `headBefore` or present on disk, replacing the bare "not tracked at `headBefore`" — which also matches rule 6's own stated conservatism ("a repo with case-variant filenames cannot move both in one reply"). #12 keeps its discrimination with the Linux half restated as "refused at rule 5's tracked clause" against macOS's disk clause; since the validator messages already name the offending pair, add the clause they name so that contrast is observable, and extend #2 with the pair (README.md tracked, `notes.md` → `readme.md`) as a Linux rejection.

findings.location: Chosen design / Read-only git — "`git()`'s env pins a fixed pipeline author and committer"
findings.problem: new: the mechanism is named but the value is not, and it is an externally visible output on every platform row — every stage commit in every run, including the dogfood acceptance that inspects `git show --name-status -M` and the review prompts that read `git log`, carries one identity that no operator can configure because global and system config are suppressed.
findings.fix: Name it in the same sentence — e.g. GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/GIT_COMMITTER_NAME = `bindforge`, GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL/GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL = a fixed pipeline address — and state it as env on `git()` (all four vars) rather than `-c user.*` on the two authoring calls, so the identity is one documented constant instead of an implementation choice.

findings.location: Chosen design — Read-only git (item 5) — "A hit ends the stage as `git-plant-detected: <path>`, escalating to the operator like `moves-rollback-failed`: no attempt 2 and no finalize, since both would run in that worktree under the planted config and the `since` window never re-detects it."
findings.problem: new. Escalation is not git-free in this runner, so the new terminal class neutralizes nothing: the escalation path ends in `finalizeEscalate`, which writes ESCALATION.md and then calls `commitStage` (runner.ts:2008-2013) — `git add -A` (298) and `git commit -m` (307, no `--no-verify`) in the same worktree; the review-pass escalation path likewise still sweeps (`finalizeReviewPass(..., false)` at runner.ts:1313, whose own comment at 1089-1091 says "the sweep still runs") via `git rev-parse`/`git status`/`git restore` (180, 213, 236). So the act of escalating is itself a runner-privilege git call over the plant: `git add -A` refreshes the index and fires a planted `core.fsmonitor`, and `git commit` executes a planted `.git/hooks/pre-commit`. #13's new containment assertion — "with the plant in place the runner's next git call must not execute it — the hostile config is a `core.fsmonitor` that touches a marker file, which stays absent" — fails against the design as written, and the paragraph's own note that "the `since` window never re-detects it" leaves the plant live for an operator `pipeline resume` (runner.ts:1376) too.
findings.fix: Name the neutralization that runs before any git on this path: the runner deletes the detected `.git` path (or pins `-c core.fsmonitor=false -c core.hooksPath=<empty dir>` on the escalation-path calls). Replace "no finalize, since both would run in that worktree under the planted config" with that step, make #13's marker fixture assert it against `finalizeEscalate`'s commit rather than a bare "next git call", and state what `resume` requires of the operator (nothing in-process clears the plant).

findings.location: Chosen design — Read-only git (item 5) + Test strategy #13 — "The same two configs append a `subagent` deny: the audit judges one attempt's own message list, and gates.ts:257 names subagents as the route around config denies" / "every completed `.git` write (`src/.git/config` plant, `git log --output=.git/config`, a subagent-launched one) escalates the stage"
findings.problem: re-raised. The `subagent` deny is real progress, but the ship gate now asserts what the named mechanism cannot produce. The audit reads `lastSeen`, the one session id the attempt polled (runner.ts:745-769, 839; independence.ts:11 "its own message list"); no text names anything that enumerates the attempt's child sessions and feeds their completed `write`/`edit`/`patch`/shell parts into the matcher. With the deny in force the launch is refused, so there is no child write part to escalate; with the deny routed around — the case the paragraph exists for, since it opens "agent-config permissions are only advisory" — the child's `.git` write is invisible to the audit and the stage commits under it. Either way #13's subagent case cannot pass as an audit assertion, and the paragraph still claims runner-side enforcement over "the plant the sweep cannot see or undo".
findings.fix: Pick one and say it in one clause. (a) Add the enumeration the assertion presumes — the runner walks the attempt's child sessions reached from its completed `task` parts and runs the same matcher over their parts — and keep #13's case; or (b) drop "a subagent-launched one" from #13's escalate list, keep it in the refused-by-config list, and record the subagent route as covered by the advisory config deny only (audit-blind) in both the paragraph and the Risks row.

findings.location: Chosen design — Read-only git (item 5) — "`git()` (runner.ts:106-112) stops reading ambient config — `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` at an empty file … so the outside-repo config sources A6 names never execute at runner privilege" (and the Risks row's "nothing outside the repo executes at runner privilege")
findings.problem: new. The blanket scope is wider than the one helper that ships the env. Two other runner git spawns bypass `git()`: `gitOk` (runner.ts:143-145, which serves `blobStamp`'s `git cat-file -e`) and the `merge-base` call at runner.ts:1417-1420, both plain `spawnSync('git', …)` inheriting the operator's environment. #13's "A hostile `~/.gitconfig` never runs" and "a stage commit lands in a tmpRepo holding no global or system config at all" therefore pin only part of the runner's git surface, and the committer-identity pin likewise lives only in `git()`.
findings.fix: Scope the claim to `git()`'s calls, or make it "every runner git call" and name the shared env helper that `gitOk` and the `merge-base` call go through.

findings.location: Chosen design — Read-only git (item 5) + Compatibility matrix — "a bare repo planted in the worktree is already inert, because `git()` pins `cwd: repoDir`" / "floor set by `safe.bareRepository=explicit`, which the runner's git env passes"
findings.problem: re-raised. The rewrite fixed the mis-attribution I asked about but left the flag orphaned: per git-config, `explicit` only refuses a bare repository discovered at the invocation's own cwd, and `git()`'s cwd is pinned with `.git` present there, so no sentence in the design now claims anything the flag guards — while the git ≥ 2.38 floor still rests on it and #13's "a bare repo planted in the worktree is never the discovered repo" passes with or without the flag.
findings.fix: Either state the one case the flag does guard — `repoDir` itself turned into a bare repo (root-level `config`/`HEAD`/`objects/`, the only in-worktree config landing with no `.git` segment, invisible to the narrowed predicate and the audit) — and add that case to #13; or drop the flag and set the floor from the oldest feature actually used (`--no-optional-locks`).

findings.location: Chosen design — Validator rule 7 — "rule 2's `.git` segment test then runs on the resolved path made relative to that realpath, so a checkout under a `project.git` ancestor stays legal"
findings.problem: new. The relativization is the fix r1 asked for, but its stated reason went stale in the same revision: with the predicate narrowed to `.git` segment equality, `project.git` never matched it, so the "so" attributes legality to the wrong mechanism, and no test pins that layout (#13's `git worktree add` exercises the pointer-file case, not a `*.git` ancestor).
findings.fix: End the sentence at "…made relative to that realpath"; if the bare-clone-with-worktrees layout matters, pin it as a rule 2/7 case in Test strategy #2.

findings.location: Options considered — "**Agent git access, any scope.** Rejected … No named-command allowlist fixes that half"
findings.problem: new. The Non-goals line was narrowed this round to "Any agent git write access, any scope", which is what the design ships against; the unchanged Options heading and its last sentence now read as rejecting the four-command read-only allowlist the Chosen design ships (item 5).
findings.fix: One clause: the rejection is of write-capable agent git access, and the read-only allowlist ships only with the audit plus `git()`'s config-free env — the same split ADR-005's Alternatives plus its item 5 make.

findings.location: Test strategy #13 — "every completed `.git` write (`src/.git/config` plant, `git log --output=.git/config`, a subagent-launched one) escalates the stage with no attempt 2"
findings.problem: new: the parenthetical pins the wrong mechanism. The design's own sentence two paragraphs earlier states "the audit judges one attempt's own message list" (independence.ts audits one session's `lastSeen` with the `since` window), so a write completed in a child session is never in the matcher's input; and with "any subagent launch is refused by the agent config" pinned one clause earlier, a subagent-launched write cannot even reach completed state in the same fixture. The gate clause is unimplementable as written — or silently assumes child-session scanning the Chosen design never specifies, which changes the audit's scope contract.
findings.fix: Drop "a subagent-launched one" from the audit-escalation list — the preceding clause, "any subagent launch is refused by the agent config", already pins that vector — or add one sentence making the audit walk the child sessions the attempt spawned, naming which message lists it reads.

findings.location: Chosen design — Read-only git: "The same two configs append a `subagent` deny" vs Risks row 1: "escalates the stage to the operator for any `.git`-segment write, however spelled"
findings.problem: new: the subagent deny ships only on the two item-5 configs, but the audit matcher runs "over every attempt" and the doc's own Deferred bullet (and its code-correctness.md:27-31 citation) says the review/research/doc-sync seats already run `git diff*` and `git log*` in writable worktrees. Nothing denies those seats `subagent`, and the carrier cannot see child-session writes, so a hostile non-item-5 seat can route a `.git` config plant through a child session past both controls: the sweep cannot see it (A4) and the next runner git call re-reads it, while row 1 claims "any" `.git`-segment write escalates.
findings.fix: Append the same `subagent` deny to every seat whose shell can write the worktree, or scope the row-1 mitigation to the item-5 seats and state explicitly that subagent routing from the non-item-5 seats sits on the Deferred sandbox line.

reply.summary: All six findings consumed by changing the design, not appending. (1) major — escalation- neutralizes-nothing: the paragraph no longer claims "no finalize, since both would run under the planted config"; it names what runs before any git on the escalation path (`finalizeEscalate` → `commitStage`, runner.ts:2008-2013) and pins the plant inert via `-c core.fsmonitor=false -c core.hooksPath=<empty dir>`, states that nothing in-process clears the plant so `pipeline resume` (1376) runs over it until the operator removes it, and #13's marker fixture now asserts against that commit instead of a bare "next git call". (2) major — chose fix (b): the subagent enumeration was NOT added; "a subagent-launched one" is deleted from #13's audit-escalation list, stays in the refused-by-config list, and the paragraph plus Risks row now state the audit reads one attempt's own session, so child writes are audit-blind and covered by the advisory `subagent` deny only. (3) minor — the env is now one shared env over every runner git call, naming `gitOk` (143-145) and the raw `merge-base` spawn (1417-1420), and #13 pins those calls. (4) minor — `safe.bareRepository=explicit` deleted; the git floor is re-set to ≥ 2.32 from `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`, the nested-bare claim stays attributed to the pinned `cwd: repoDir`, and the one case the flag did guard (config landing at the worktree root with no `.git` segment) is handed to the Deferred sandbox line instead of designed in. (5) nit — rule 7's stale "so a checkout under a `project.git` ancestor stays legal" deleted. (6) nit — Options heading and closing clause narrowed to write-capable agent git access, so they no longer reject the read-only allowlist that ships. Also removed the duplicated ship-gate sentence (now owned by #13) and the duplicated subagent/audit clause. Net +1 line (335→336), because naming the escalation commit, the shared env's members, and the resume consequence for the two majors costs more than the deletions in rule 7, Options 5, the ship-gate sentence and the deny clause pay back.
reply.commitMessage: docs: pin git plants inert across every runner git call in the moves proposal

findings.location: Chosen design — Read-only git (item 5) — "`git()`'s env (106-112) becomes the shared env for every runner git call — `gitOk` (143-145) and the raw `merge-base` spawn (1417-1420) included"
findings.problem: re-raised. My r1 env-scope finding is partly closed — the text now claims "every runner git call" and names gitOk and merge-base, and #13, the Risks row and the Compatibility row follow — but the enumeration still misses a fourth spawn site: `writeEditorialDiff` (called from runner.ts:1507 in the review/editorial loop) runs `spawnSync('git', ['diff','--no-index',…], {cwd: repoDir})` at runner.ts:1933-1937, outside `git()`/`gitOk`, inheriting the operator's environment and reading the worktree's config. So the absolute claim in the paragraph and in #13's gate ("every runner git call, `gitOk` and `merge-base` included") is false as written, and an implementer who treats the list as exhaustive leaves that call un-pinned.
findings.fix: Name all non-`git()` sites: "`gitOk` (143-145), the raw `merge-base` spawn (1417-1420) and `writeEditorialDiff`'s `git diff --no-index` (1933-1937) included", and add the editorial-diff call to #13's "every runner git call" list; or state the rule as "every `spawnSync('git')` site goes through the one env helper", which keeps the claim true as sites change.

findings.location: Chosen design — Read-only git (item 5) — "So neither the config sources outside the repo (A6) nor a planted `.git/config` or `.git/hooks` runs at runner privilege" (and the Risks row's "nothing outside the repo executes at runner privilege")
findings.problem: new. The conclusion is wider than the mechanism named two sentences earlier. `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM`/`GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` suppress only the system and per-user levels (I confirmed against git(1): setting GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL means neither $HOME/.gitconfig nor $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config is read), and `-c core.fsmonitor=false -c core.hooksPath=<empty dir>` overrides exactly two keys; the repo-local `.git/config` is still read, and A6 — cited in this same paragraph — states config is also read via "`include.path` from any of them". A planted `.git/config` with `[include] path = /home/<operator>/.gitconfig` re-opens the outside-repo sources at runner privilege, and other exec-capable repo-local keys that fire in the escalation's own git calls (e.g. `filter.<driver>.clean` under `git add -A` at runner.ts:298, selected by a planted `.gitattributes`, which is not a `.git` segment and so is neither config-denied nor audit-matched) are untouched by the pins. #13's fsmonitor-marker fixture passes while the blanket guarantee stays false.
findings.fix: Scope the sentence to what ships: "neither the system nor per-user config sources A6 names are read, and the two A6 mechanisms that fire in these calls — `core.fsmonitor` on an index refresh and hooks — are overridden; other exec-capable repo-local keys (filters, external diff) and an `include.path` inside a planted `.git/config` are the Deferred sandbox's" — or add the pins that would make the blanket form true.

findings.location: Chosen design — Read-only git (item 5) — closing sentences of the paragraph (previously "If Test strategy #13 lets a vector land a plant, or a runner git call run over one, the change does not merge.")
findings.problem: new. This revision dropped the merge-blocking clause. Goals still promises item 5 lands "conditional on the controls and ship gate named under Read-only git", and #13 still labels itself "Item 5's ship gate asserts containment, not just detection", but the section that names the gate no longer states its consequence, so the condition the Goals row relies on has no stated effect.
findings.fix: Restore the one sentence at the end of the paragraph: "If Test strategy #13 lets a vector land a plant, or a runner git call run over one, the change does not merge."

findings.location: Chosen design — Read-only git: "So neither the config sources outside the repo (A6) nor a planted `.git/config` or `.git/hooks` runs at runner privilege"; Test strategy #13: "the hostile config is a `core.fsmonitor` touching a marker file, which stays absent"
findings.problem: new: the revision replaced the r1 posture I approved ("no attempt 2 and no finalize, since both would run in that worktree under the planted config") with one that runs git over the live plant — the escalation's own ESCALATION.md commit and every pipeline resume — justified by an inertness claim the pinned env does not deliver. GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM and GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL suppress only outside-repo sources; the -c pins cover exactly core.fsmonitor and core.hooksPath. The planted root .git/config — precisely #13's own `git log --output=.git/config` case, which the sweep cannot see or undo (A4) — remains the discovered repo-local config every runner git call reads at runner privilege, and its other exec-capable keys survive: `alias.status = '!…'` (git expands aliases at the first non-option argument, shadowing builtins) or `filter.evil.clean = '!…'` paired with a stage-owned .gitattributes (clean filters run at commitStage's `git add -A`). #13 pins a single hostile key (fsmonitor), so the ship gate passes with the alias/filter vectors open.
findings.fix: Either restore the r1 posture — on `git-plant-detected` no runner git call runs over the infected worktree (replaces the escalation-commit sentence and row 1's "the plant pinned inert before the escalation's own commit") — or scope the claim to the two pinned keys, move the unplanted keys (`alias.*`, `filter.<driver>.clean`, `diff.external`) onto the Deferred sandbox line, and extend #13's hostile config with one of them (e.g. `filter.evil.clean` matching a stage-written `.gitattributes`, marker stays absent across the escalation's `git add -A`) so the gate pins the claim the design makes.

findings.location: Chosen design — Read-only git: "a child agent's `.git` write is audit-blind and the `subagent` deny below is the only cover for that route"; Risks row 1: "child-agent writes are audit-blind, covered by the advisory `subagent` deny only"
findings.problem: re-raised: closure of my r1 finding 2 is incomplete. The deny ships on "the same two configs" (the item-5 seats) only, while the doc's own allowlist parenthetical ("review seats already run the same two of four, `git diff*` and `git log*`") keeps non-item-5 seats running git in a writable worktree with no `subagent` deny — for those seats the child-session `.git` route has zero cover, not "the deny only", and it is placed nowhere: the widened Deferred sandbox bullet covers only "config writes landing outside the worktree or at its root with no `.git` segment", which an in-worktree `.git`-segment plant is not.
findings.fix: One clause on the Deferred sandbox bullet placing the non-item-5 seats' child-session `.git` route there (the r1 ask, still unmade), or extend the `subagent` deny to every seat whose shell can write the worktree.

findings.location: Compatibility matrix, git row — "floor set by `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` (introduced in git 2.32)"
findings.problem: new (created by this revision): the floor was lowered 2.38 → 2.32 in the same round that put `-c core.fsmonitor=false` into the shared git env, so the row now claims uniform support for a band in which one of its own pins does not mean what the row implies. git's config documentation warns for `core.fsmonitor`: "Git versions 2.35.1 and prior will not understand the boolean values and will consider the \"true\" or \"false\" values as hook pathnames to be invoked. Git versions 2.26 thru 2.35.1 default to hook protocol V2 and will fall back to no fsmonitor (full scan)". So across the newly claimed band (2.32–2.35.1) the pin is read as a hook path rather than an off switch — it still shadows a planted value (command-line `-c` outranks repo-local config) but disables nothing by name — and Test strategy #13's marker-file assertion runs only against CI's git, so the band the matrix calls `yes` is unexercised and unlabeled, unlike the macOS row.
findings.fix: Set the floor at the version where every pin in the shared env has the meaning the row implies (git's boolean `core.fsmonitor` reading), re-justifying the row as "floor set by `core.fsmonitor`'s boolean value; `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` (2.32), `core.hooksPath` (2.9), `--no-optional-locks` and `git cat-file -t` all predate it", and update the Revision log's 2.32 line to match. To keep 2.32 instead, state the fallback in the row — below the boolean reading the pin shadows the planted value as an uninvokable hook path and git falls back to a full index scan — and name in #13 the git version the ship gate ran on, marking the band below it unverified the way the macOS row is.

findings.location: Chosen design / Read-only git — "`git()`'s env (106-112) becomes the shared env for every runner git call — `gitOk` (143-145) and the raw `merge-base` spawn (1417-1420) included — setting `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` at an empty file, `-c core.fsmonitor=false -c core.hooksPath=<empty dir>`, and a fixed pipeline author and committer replacing the identity that env suppresses"
findings.problem: re-raised: my r1 fix's mechanism half landed (one shared env over every runner git call), the value half did not. The identity is still unnamed while the matrix row still sells it as platform-visible ("that env pins a fixed pipeline committer identity, so no operator `~/.gitconfig` is needed to land a stage commit"), and it is an output every dogfood check (`git show --name-status -M`) and review prompt (`git log`) reads — a constant no operator can configure, since global and system config are suppressed. The rewritten sentence also now files two `-c` command-line flags under the word "env", and `<empty dir>` is a new on-disk artifact named nowhere else in the document although every platform row must supply it.
findings.fix: In that one sentence name `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME`/`GIT_COMMITTER_NAME` = `bindforge` and `GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL`/`GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL` = one fixed pipeline address; move the two `-c` flags into a separate "and `-c` on every call" clause so "env" names only env; and name the empty hooks directory the runner creates (and where, outside the worktree) in place of the `<empty dir>` placeholder.

findings.location: Chosen design, Validator rule 7 — "rule 2's `.git` segment test then runs on the resolved path relative to that realpath."
findings.problem: new (deletion in this revision): the clause that followed — "so a checkout under a `project.git` ancestor stays legal" — was dropped. The behavior is still specified, but that example was the only text making its purpose observable: read alone, rule 2 ("no endpoint `.git`-denied") plus rule 7 are satisfied by a predicate scanning absolute paths, which refuses every move in a repo checked out under an ancestor whose name ends in `.git` (a `git clone …/foo.git` layout). Test strategy #2's `.git` endpoint assertions all place the offending segment inside the repo, so none would catch that platform-layout change.
findings.fix: Restore the deleted consequence in the same sentence rather than adding new rule text — "…relative to that realpath, so a checkout under a `*.git` ancestor stays legal" — and, if the pin is wanted, add one legal-pair case to #2 in a tmpRepo whose ancestor ends in `.git`, which is the assertion that keeps the relative form from being implemented as an absolute one.

findings.location: Options considered, "Allow directory moves" — "file-only drops that whole rule class."
findings.problem: re-raised: the r1 wording was compressed but the overclaim survived. The rule class is not dropped whole — validator rule 6 still carries "no listed path a path-prefix of another," which is needed for file pairs (e.g. to1=a with to2=a/b), and rule 4's tracked-at-headBefore check still exists in file form. An implementer could read the rationale as license to drop the prefix clause. The Revision log records no rejection of this finding, and the revision pass rewrote the sentence without narrowing it.
findings.fix: Replace "file-only drops that whole rule class" with "file-only drops the self-containment-as-directory-rule, the cascade rules, and the per-child tracked-at-headBefore check; rule 6's path-prefix clause stays for file pairs."

findings.location: Chosen design → Apply — "Immediately before the first rename it re-runs rules 4–7 as one guard across the inference→finalize window"
findings.problem: re-raised, amplified by the revision. The new apply guard re-executes validator rules 4–7 a second time for every successful move stage, re-incurring the unbatched per-pair git spawn cost flagged at r1: rule 4's `git cat-file -t <headBefore>:<from>` per pair and rule 5's per-`to` headBefore membership query. My r1 note covered only the reply-validation pass (repeated on nudge cycles and attempt 2); the revision adds a mandatory second full pass on the happy path, doubling the spawns. The new `.max(64)` caps n but not the per-pair spawn count: worst case ≈ 2×128 subprocess spawns per finalize (≈ 2×46 for run 004's 23-pair payload, A12). Finalize-time and off any keystroke/event path, so minor — but the revisions made an open cost finding worse without acknowledging it.
findings.fix: Read headBefore once per stage, not once per rule pass: one `git ls-tree -r --name-only <headBefore>` snapshot (or `git cat-file --batch` fed all `<headBefore>:<path>` endpoint queries) consumed by both `validateMoves` and the apply guard. headBefore is an immutable commit, so the tree read is shareable across passes while the disk-dependent halves of rules 4–7 (existsSync, parent existence, realpath) still re-run at apply. Replaces the per-pair `git cat-file -t` in rule 4 and the per-`to` tracked lookup in rule 5 with one spawn per stage.

findings.location: Chosen design — Read-only git: "So neither the config sources outside the repo (A6) nor a planted `.git/config` or `.git/hooks` runs at runner privilege" (also "the plant is inert before any git there" / "a `pipeline resume` … runs over it until the operator removes it"); Risks row 1: "the plant pinned inert before the escalation's own commit — pinned by #13"; Test strategy #13: "the hostile config is a `core.fsmonitor` touching a marker file, which stays absent"
findings.problem: re-raised (unchanged): the dissent diff names one blob twice, so no section changed since r2 and the Revision log carries no entry answering this finding; the recorded r3 rationale — "the plant pinned inert before the escalation's own commit by one config-free env over every runner git call" — is itself unsound. findings.location: Chosen design — Validator, rule 4: "`git ls-tree <headBefore> -- <from>` mode 100644/100755 — this is the file-only rule; trees and mode-120000 symlinks fail it"
findings.problem: The r4 rewrite's command does not test the entry itself when `from` is a tree. git-ls-tree treats `<path>` as a match pattern, and without `-d` ("show only the named tree entry itself, not its children") it lists a matched directory's children — so `git ls-tree <head> -- src` emits 100644/100755 lines for a directory whose children are regular files, and an implementation that literally checks the mode of the ls-tree output accepts a directory, breaking the file-only rule rule 4 exists to enforce. The glob-pattern nature of the path argument compounds it (rule 1 allows `*`, `?`, `[`). Test strategy #2's "`from` a tree" pin catches a naive implementation, so behavior is pinned, but the rule text specifies a command that does not do the stated job by construction.
findings.fix: In rule 4, specify `git ls-tree -d <headBefore> -- <from>` (one line, the entry itself; modes 100644/100755 pass, 040000 tree and 120000 symlink fail), or state that the validator requires exactly one output line whose path field equals `from` before applying the mode test. This replaces the current command invocation only; nothing else in rule 4 or the Compatibility row changes.
